title: Posole Verde
subtitle: Green chicken and white bean stew
excerpt: Posole is a Mexican stew built around hominy, the dried corn kernel treated with alkali to soften it. Cannellini beans make a practical and similar substitute, giving the broth the same starchy body. This version uses green chilli and plenty of coriander for a fresh, bright result.
sourceNotes: Posole has been eaten in Mexico since pre-Columbian times, originally as a ceremonial food made with maize. The word comes from the Nahuatl pozol and the dish remains a staple for celebrations and family gatherings across Mexico.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze without the avocado garnish for up to 3 months.

content.text: Blending the tinned tomatoes before adding gives the broth a smooth, even body rather than chunks of tomato. A stick blender in the tin works well.

items.prepNote: 2 x 400g tins, drained and rinsed, as a hominy substitute
green variety if available, otherwise standard; blended to a smooth sauce

content.text: Place the chicken thighs, stock, onion, garlic, oregano, and a generous pinch of salt in the stockpot. Bring to the boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer. Cook for 30 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Remove the chicken with tongs and shred it using two forks. Strain and reserve the poaching stock, discarding the onion and garlic solids.
Return the strained stock to the pot. Add the blended tinned tomatoes and the drained cannellini beans. Bring back to a simmer.
Return the shredded chicken to the pot. Simmer for 20 minutes until the beans have absorbed the flavour of the broth and the soup has thickened slightly.
Stir in most of the coriander. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and a squeeze of lime. Ladle into bowls and top each with sliced avocado, the remaining coriander, and lime wedges to squeeze over.

items.cause: The stew needs longer to reduce, or more beans to add body
items.fix: Mash a handful of beans against the side of the pot to release their starch, then stir them back in. Simmer uncovered for 10 more minutes.
Keep the poach at a bare simmer rather than a rolling boil. The chicken only needs 30 minutes.
